ownership.created: Geometry, cloned/default materials and instancing GPU allocations; dispose once through returned dispose().
ownership.borrowed: Host Three namespace and textures/maps. Supplied materials are cloned as owned adapters; originals and maps remain unchanged and undisposed.

overhangBounds.meaning: Conservative bounds of all above-deck geometry, including porch cornices, rails and urns; not gameplay collision.

appearance.palette: Warm ivory painted finish, muted olive/slate roof, teal glazing, brown leaves and striped awnings are game choices; historical colours unresolved.
appearance.uv: Original native BoxGeometry UV/positions/normals retained. Separate grossUV uses metres. Native walls and all authored planar triangles, including sloped roofs, have metric UVs; curved turned ornaments use local projections/circumference approximations.
appearance.mapPeriod: Caller supplies repeat-ready maps. Reviews use a 2 m period (repeat .5) for existing facade and roof maps; keep a consistent period when replacing a skin. Texture transforms are never mutated.

defaultTextureTransfer.note: Default material mixes inherited map with the base painted colour in linear space. Borrowed material adapters preserve the supplied material response (blend1). These transfers are reproduced in CPU export.

physicalMaterial.reason: Monochrome plates establish appearance; combustion properties require later content evidence.

source.creator: McKim, Mead & White
source.rights: Cached IA metadata possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Credit architects, publication and Getty scan; no source image is a runtime asset.
source.publicationDate: Later publication of original 1893 building. Title spans 1879-1915; IA catalogue1914 discrepancy remains unresolved.

adaptations: Rear opening rhythm and service faces
Roof plan, depth, back joins and tower back faces

integration: Separate exterior landmark at full scale; not placed into the 51 m street. Gameplay, interiors, collision, fire, traversal and runtime browser acceptance remain later work.
